assertions_contracts.best_practice: The php.net manual's assert page (verified this pass) documents zend.assertions: 1 generates and executes assertion code, 0 generates but skips it, -1 does not generate code at all (production mode). External rejection must therefore be an explicit throw, exactly as the guide prescribes.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Upgraded from run 1's unverified: the manual's zend.assertions table was fetched via search of the php.net manual this pass and confirms -1 means assertions are not even compiled. The guide's section 5 states the same mechanism accurately.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert() only for programmer invariants; external validation by explicit throw, explicitly because zend.assertions=-1 strips assertions in production (guide section 5, SKILL workflow step 3).

bounded_work.best_practice: Still current; no official guidance endorses unbounded remote reads or retries, and nothing in the 8.5 line changes the obligation.
bounded_work.evidence: Uncontradicted by the php.net sources fetched live this pass (supported versions, 8.5 release announcement). Tiger policy stricter than default by design.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named bounds for input bytes, JSON depth, items, retries with shared deadline/backoff/jitter; memory_limit as backstop only (guide section 6).

concurrency.best_practice: Still accurate for current PHP; the 8.4/8.5 lines did not change the fiber model or the worker caveat. PHP 8.5's persistent cURL share handles (handles surviving across requests) reinforce, rather than relax, the guide's warning that worker-mode state persists.
concurrency.evidence: Supported-versions table and the 8.5 release announcement were fetched live this pass; neither contradicts the guide's fiber/worker framing.
concurrency.guide_position: Fibers (8.1+) cooperative not parallel; bound fiber counts; long-running workers (RoadRunner/FrankenPHP) break shared-nothing, reset per request (guide sections 13 and 20).

error_handling.best_practice: Still current PHP practice; the 8.5 line adds get_error_handler()/get_exception_handler() introspection helpers but does not change exception discipline.
error_handling.evidence: The 8.5 release announcement fetched live this pass lists the new handler-introspection functions among its additions; no primary source contradicts the guide's discipline.
error_handling.guide_position: Domain exceptions, chaining with previous, no @ suppression, no casual catch Throwable, error/exception handlers at entry points (guide section 9).

formatting.best_practice: PHP-FIG PER Coding Style extends, expands and replaces PSR-12 and is the living standard (PER-CS 3.x), adding rules for enums, match, promotion, readonly, attributes and newer syntax that PSR-12 does not cover.
formatting.evidence: Narrow residual of the run-1 stale verdict. The pass-1 fix is verified in the full guide's section 24, which now names PER-CS with the extends/expands/replaces wording. But three operative surfaces still prescribe the superseded standard as the rule: SKILL.md's Formatting rule, SKILL.md's Review Checklist, and the full guide's own section 30 checklist all still say PSR-12 (verified by full-text search this pass; recorded as mechanical fixes below). PER meta document fetched live this pass confirms the replacement wording. Run-2 coordinator pass (2026-10-14): the defect behind this verdict was cured in the guide text in both trees (see mechanical_fixes, marked applied) and the aspect was re-judged on the cured text: holds.
formatting.guide_position: Guide section 24 now names PER-CS via the pass-1 fix; however SKILL.md still prescribes php-cs-fixer with PSR-12 (or Laravel Pint) in its Formatting rule and checklist, and the guide's section 30 checklist still says php-cs-fixer PSR-12. House values: 4-space, 120 columns, ordered imports.

memory_ownership.best_practice: Does not apply as an ownership aspect: PHP is reference-counted/GC; the applicable analogue is resource lifetime, which the guide addresses in section 14.
memory_ownership.evidence: Aspect does not apply in the Rust/C++ sense; do not force a finding. Verdict unchanged from run 1.
memory_ownership.guide_position: No ownership system; guide covers resource lifetime instead (one owner per handle, try/finally, no destructor reliance, generator close discipline).

security.best_practice: Still current official practice; PHP 8.5's always-available URI extension (RFC 3986 / WHATWG URL parsing) strengthens the guide's SSRF/URL-validation position rather than contradicting it.
security.evidence: The 8.5 release announcement fetched live this pass documents the URI extension as a headline feature; the guide's prohibitions are uncontradicted. The URI-extension adoption itself remains a proposal (below), not a verdict change.
security.guide_position: strict_types everywhere, === at boundaries, no unserialize/eval on untrusted data, PDO real prepares, hash_equals for secrets, password_hash, SSRF/CSRF/XSS controls (guide sections 15-19 and 22).

static_analysis.best_practice: The gate practice is current. Verified from primary releases this pass: PHPStan is on the 2.3.x line, and Psalm's stable line is 6.x with a 7.0 beta whose headline work is combined analysis including its security (taint) analysis — a capability PHPStan core does not offer, so the two analysers are not interchangeable for untrusted-flow tracking.
static_analysis.evidence: Upgraded from run 1's unverified: PHPStan 2.3.0's release page and Psalm's 7.0.0-beta21 release and v7 article were verified this pass (the article describes security analysis as a Psalm feature and combined analysis in v7). The guide still pins no analyser version and states no level beyond max/strictest, and the taint split is still unaddressed — carried as a proposal, not a verdict change.
static_analysis.guide_position: PHPStan level max or Psalm strictest as a CI gate, run before tests; no mixed escapes (guide sections 1 and 28). No version is pinned anywhere in the guide or SKILL.md, and the two analysers are treated as interchangeable.

testing.best_practice: Still current practice. PHPUnit 12's official announcement states support for metadata in doc-comments was removed and tests must use attributes; the guide's own section 27 already prefers attributes over docblock annotations for machine-read metadata, but section 28 never states the test-metadata rule.
testing.evidence: PHPUnit 12 announcement verified this pass (metadata section: doc-comment support deprecated in 11, removed in 12; attributes required). Guide section 28 is silent on metadata style — a gap, recorded as a proposal; the testing model itself holds.
testing.guide_position: PHPUnit or Pest, half adversarial, static analysis and fixer in CI before tests, Infection mutation testing where budget allows (guide section 28).

toolchain_pins.best_practice: PHP 8.3 is security-only (active support ended 31 Dec 2025; security support until 31 Dec 2027). The newest stable branch is 8.5 (released 20 Nov 2025, active until 31 Dec 2027, current patch 8.5.11), so a 2026 baseline should floor at 8.4+ and describe 8.5 as current.
toolchain_pins.evidence: The pass-1 SKILL.md compatibility fix is verified present (8.4+, 'Current stable line is PHP 8.5'). The floor move itself was a run-1 proposal and remains unapplied in the operative text, confirmed by full read this pass and by the remediation addendum's spot-verification (item 19: the floor move stays a proposal): guide section 2, the composer example, the intro and SKILL.md workflow step 1 all still floor at 8.3+, a branch the supported-versions table fetched live this pass shows has been security-only since 31 Dec 2025.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Mixed surfaces: SKILL.md's compatibility line (fixed in pass 1) requires PHP 8.4+ and names 8.5 as the current stable line, but the full guide's section 2 still states the reference targets PHP 8.3+ with a composer requirement of >=8.3, the intro still reads 'Modern PHP (8.3+)', and SKILL.md's workflow step 1 still says 'PHP 8.3+ target'. 8.4 property hooks and asymmetric visibility are allowed where they clarify.

proposals.evidence: Carried from run 1, still unapplied (verified by full read this pass: guide section 2/composer floor unchanged at 8.3+, and no 8.5 feature is mentioned anywhere in the guide or SKILL.md). The 8.5 release announcement fetched live lists the pipe operator, clone with, NoDiscard, array_first/array_last and the always-available URI extension.
proposals.proposal: Raise the floor in the operative text (guide section 2, the composer example and SKILL.md workflow step 1) from 8.3+ to 8.4+, and adopt PHP 8.5 features into the contract patterns where they earn it: pipe operator |> for validated transform pipelines, clone-with for readonly value-object withers, #[NoDiscard] on results that must be consumed, array_first/array_last, and the new URI extension for URL parsing/SSRF allowlist checks instead of parse_url string stitching.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt selectively after raising the floor to 8.4/8.5: NoDiscard and URI first (safety), pipe/clone-with as style guidance. The floor move is Matt's adoption decision; this record carries it forward unapplied.

proposals.evidence: Carried from run 1, now with the versions it asked for verified from primary releases this pass: PHPStan 2.3.0 release page; Psalm 7.0.0-beta21 release notes and the psalm.dev v7 article describing security (taint) analysis as a Psalm capability with combined analysis. The guide still treats the two analysers as interchangeable and pins neither.
proposals.proposal: Pin the current analyser majors in the guide (PHPStan 2.3.x, Psalm 6.x stable; Psalm 7 is beta, not a pin), state the exact level names, and note the taint-analysis split (Psalm offers security/taint analysis; PHPStan core does not) so security-sensitive flows pick the analyser deliberately.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: one analyser per project, named with version and level, plus Psalm taint where untrusted-flow tracking is the goal.

proposals.evidence: New in this pass, from run 1's evidence note: the official PHPUnit 12 announcement states doc-comment metadata support was removed and attributes are required; guide section 28 does not mention metadata style (its section 27 attributes preference is about application code, not tests).
proposals.proposal: State in section 28 that on PHPUnit 12+ all test metadata (#[Test], #[DataProvider], #[CoversClass], groups, etc.) must be PHP attributes, since doc-comment metadata support was removed in PHPUnit 12.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a one-line addition to section 28; it aligns the testing section with the guide's existing attributes-over-docblocks rule in section 27.
